factors.factor: The IPC Template Type definition declared 21 inputs while the sensor code supplied only 20 values to the Content Interpreter, and no mechanism existed to detect or reconcile this interface mismatch before release. This mismatch also meant the Content Validator was assessing content against the declared 21-input expectation rather than the 20 values actually supplied, so it passed content that would crash sensors.
factors.evidence: "The definition of the IPC Template Type in the Template Type Definitions file stated that it expected 21 input fields. The sensor code that invoked the Content Interpreter with Channel File 291's Template Instances supplied only 20 input values to match against." | "The Content Validator evaluated the new Template Instances. It based its assessment on the expectation that the IPC Template Type would be provided with 21 inputs. The new Template Instances were sent to sensors."

factors.factor: Automated testing used a static set of 12 test cases in which all Template Instances used a wildcard in the 21st field, so the code path reading the 21st input was never exercised and the out-of-bounds read went undetected. Testing focused on functional validation rather than input-boundary handling, and stress testing with a test Template Instance did not exercise the faulty path either.

It passed the stress test and was validated for use."

factors.factor: Latent defect was activated by a later content deployment: earlier IPC Template Instances used wildcard matching and never touched the 21st input, so the risk stayed hidden until a non-wildcard instance was introduced on July 19.
factors.evidence: "No IPC Template Instances in previous channel file versions had used the 21st input parameter field."

factors.factor: The Content Interpreter processing Rapid Response Content runs in the csagent.sys kernel driver, loaded early in boot, so an invalid memory read caused by content resulted in a system bugcheck rather than being contained.

factors.factor: The sensor code lacked bounds validation when reading the input pointer array: it checked for a NULL pointer but did not verify that the index was within the 20-element array, so the read at index 0x14 went through an invalid pointer.
factors.evidence: "The code performed a NULL pointer check, then read through the invalid pointer, resulting in the out-of-bounds read and the bugcheck."

action_items.action: Reconcile the IPC Template Type input count between the Template Type Definitions file and the sensor code so that both declare and supply the same number of inputs, and add a build-time or CI check that fails when they diverge.
Add bounds checking on all Content Interpreter input array accesses in csagent.sys so that out-of-range indices return a safe default or a logged error instead of performing an unguarded read.

Extend the Content Validator to check each Template Instance against the number of inputs the sensor actually supplies at runtime, not only the declared count in the Template Type Definitions file, and block deployment on mismatch.

Build a fuzzing and boundary-condition test suite for every Template Type that exercises every input index, including non-wildcard matching criteria and inputs beyond the currently used set, and run it in the release pipeline before any content ships.
Require that test coverage for each Template Type include Template Instances that exercise all declared input fields, and reject test plans that rely on a static set of wildcard-only cases.

Evaluate whether Rapid Response Content parsing can be moved to user-mode or isolated from the kernel driver's boot-time code path, or otherwise contained so a content defect cannot crash the system at boot-level privilege.
